newsitem.title: USA: Outboard sees modestly improved 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: Outboard sees modestly improved 1997 sales.

text.p: Outboard Marine Corp said it continues to believe that retail sales will improve modestly in 1997, following a first quarter report that saw the boatmaker's net loss widen and profit margin fall.
Outboard Marine said its gross margin on the quarter fell to 11.5 percent from 17 percent in the year-ago quarter.
The company said Friday it lost $14.3 million in the first quarter, compared with a year-ago loss of $12.4 million.
At the same time, Outboard said selling, general and administrative expenses were $42.4 million in the first quarter, down 7.2 percent from a year earlier.
The company's first quarter ended December 31.

"The continuing softness in marine engine and boat sales in the fall months kept dealer inventories relatively high and resulted in a decline in OMC's sales and operating results in the quarter just ended," said chief executive Harry Bowman.

He said the results for the quarter were expected. "We suspended production of many of our larger engines for nearly a month in order to make changes to equipment," Bowman said. "This resulted in sales decreases and unabsorbed costs which constituted the largest part of the negative comparison to results for the comparative quarter last year."
He added that higher promotional expenses stemming from "rationalizing our boat brands and models" resulted in higher promotional expenses in the quarter.
Marketing and promotion costs were up on programs to launch the company's new FICHT fuel injection engines.
"The new engines, which began production during the quarter, became available on schedule and in the planned volume to the retail marine market this month," Outboard said.
The company's first quarter operating loss was $19.7 million, compared with a loss of $6.3 million a year before.

"After taking into account $1.6 million in gains from the sale of assets during the quarter and an insurance recovery of $6.1 million in an environmental matter, OMC posted a first quarter pre-tax loss of $13.5 million compared to a pre-tax loss of $11.4 million" a year ago, Outboard said.
"Despite weaker than expected market conditions heading into the winter boat show season, we continue to believe there will be modestly improved retail sales in 1997," it said.

"We have begun to see benefits from our 1996 reengineering projects and are encouraged by the initial phases of the larger scale earnings improvement initiatives we have undertaken this year," Bowman said.
